questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Looking at the tire is good enough.
Squeeze the tire to check it.
Compare how tall the tire is to another tire.

questions.explanation: Always use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before riding. A tire that is not fully inflated may still look fine, so you cannot trust just looking at it.

questions.question: The best source of information for your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone who owns a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read your owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. It tells you about the specific features of your bike.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait an hour for each drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still feel effects from the alcohol.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still feel effects from the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can build up in your system even if you drink only one drink per hour. Your ability to ride and your judgment can still be impaired.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects the wearer from:
questions.explanation: Besides protecting your face from injury in a crash, a face shield keeps out wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and small rocks thrown up by other vehicles.

questions.question: For the best protection, riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another tough material to protect your hands.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they distract you.
Should be avoided since other drivers will see you easily.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: For safety, you need to know what is behind you. Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning routine.

questions.question: When consuming alcohol:

options.text: Your body is mostly unaffected until you reach the legal intoxication limit.
Negative effects are usually minimal until you reach the legal intoxication limit.
Your ability to drive and ride is affected well before the legal intoxication limit.
There is nothing to worry about if you drink only one or two drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your ability to drive and ride is affected well before the legal intoxication limit.
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs your riding and driving ability long before you reach the legal limit. Even one drink can cause serious impairment.

questions.question: When riding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
Use only the front brake when stopping.
Use only the rear brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down. Use both brakes when stopping and avoid making quick changes in speed or direction.

questions.question: Unlike most food and drinks, alcohol does not need to be digested. This means that:

options.text: The alcohol reaches your brain within minutes and starts to affect you.
The alcohol never leaves your body.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of the alcohol quickly once it is in your system.

questions.correctAnswerText: The alcohol reaches your brain within minutes and starts to affect you.
questions.explanation: Because it does not need to be digested, alcohol enters your bloodstream quickly and reaches your brain within minutes. Your body removes alcohol slowly—about one drink per hour.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface, what should you do?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down. Use both brakes and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator slow down?
questions.explanation: Downshifting slows a motorcycle. However, downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT check on your tires?
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. How can you be more visible?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright colors while riding, even during the day.

questions.question: How does keeping space around your motorcycle help you?

options.text: Give you space to react to hazards.
Allow you to look at road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you space to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT check on your tires before riding?
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: Which item does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Boots that go over the ankle
A baseball cap that fits snugly

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: For protection, wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and pants, high boots that cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Who is most likely to have a crash?

options.text: Those who have completed a safety course.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often with untrained, beginning riders who are not familiar with their motorcycle.

questions.question: For the best protection, your helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all around and have no obvious defects.

questions.question: If your motorcycle will take longer to stop than usual, what should you do?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, increase your following distance. If your motorcycle needs more time to stop, stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.question: You should check your motorcycle completely:
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Check your motorcycle completely before every ride.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Keep your intentions unknown from other drivers.
Always stay within a foot of another vehicle.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals and brake light. Position your motorcycle properly. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
Only have one set of footrests.
Not encourage the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other motorists that a passenger is on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Only carry a passenger if your motorcycle has a seat for two riders. Your motorcycle should have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear you wear.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If you can, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, which increases danger.
